title: Zetta Retail — POC model scoping & multilingual requirements
summary: POC scoping focused on open-model shortlist for multilingual retail+support workloads, success criteria (latency p95, accuracy on attribute extraction, cost targets), dataset sizing and benchmarks, timeline for 3-week pilot and required infra (dedicated vs hosted). Action items: Redwood to share model shortlist + benchmark plan and security docs; Zetta to share sample dataset and acceptance tests.
topics: Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
next_steps: Jordan: Share shortlist + proposed benchmark harness and rough cost estimates (by 2025-09-02)
Aisha: Upload 5-10k sample records + evaluation labels to shared bucket (by 2025-09-04)
Priya: Schedule a 60-min kickoff to start the pilot run (week of 2025-09-08)
Jordan: Share SOC2 + security overview and network options (by 2025-09-01)
action_items: Jordan Kim — send model shortlist csv + benchmark plan — due 2025-09-02
Aisha Rahman — drop sample dataset (catalog + chat logs) to S3 and share link — due 2025-09-04
Priya Nair — prepare runner for p95 latency and token-cost reporting — due 2025-09-06
Sam Li — confirm VPC peering requirements and firewall rules — due 2025-09-05
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making the time. Quick roll call?
[00:04] Miguel (CTO): Miguel here.
[00:06] Aisha (Head of ML): Aisha on the line.
[00:08] Sam (SRE): Sam.
[00:09] Eva (Product): Eva.
[00:11] Priya (SE): Priya from Redwood. Hi all.
[00:13] Jordan: Cool. Agenda: short discovery, success criteria, model shortlist for the POC, benchmarks, and timelines.
[00:22] Miguel: Sounds good. We're trying to pick an open model for an end-to-end POC: product attribute extraction, SKU normalization, and a store-support chat assistant across EN/ES/FR. Security and cost are big constraints.
[00:35] Jordan: Understood. Can you quantify traffic and latency expectations?
[00:39] Eva: We're looking at peak 40 RPS across all channels initially, steady-state maybe 10 RPS. Latency we want sub-300 ms p95 ideally for assistant calls, and for batch attribute extraction we can tolerate higher.
[00:52] Priya: Okay, that's helpful. Are you planning real-time KV cache re-use or mostly stateless calls?
[00:58] Sam: We'll have conversation context for the chat flows — so KV cache matters — for ingestion jobs it's batch.
[01:05] Aisha: Accuracy targets: for attribute extraction we'd like F1 > 0.88 on our labeled set; for chat intent classification > 90% top-1. Cost target is roughly $X per 10k tokens — we gave a rough internal number but need Redwood to map actual model costs.
[01:22] Jordan: We'll produce a shortbench that reports p50/p95 latency, throughput, token-cost, and an accuracy pass/fail per model. For the shortlist we typically propose a couple of quantized medium-sized models and one larger baseline.
[01:34] Miguel: Which open models are you thinking? We prefer open to avoid licensing friction.
[01:38] Priya: Tentative shortlist for this POC: Llama2-13B-q4 (quantized), MPT-30B-Instruct (int8), Falcon-40B-instruct (float16 baseline), and a smaller distilled model for edge cases like Falcon-7B or a 7B Llama derivative for very low cost. We can also add an EU-hosted LLM variant if data residency becomes a hard req.
[01:58] Aisha: Any concerns around multilingual quality? Spanish is very important; French is secondary. Some open models have weaker ES/FR.
[02:06] Priya: Right. Falcon historically has decent multilingual understanding but lower instruction tuning on some languages; Llama family is generally good at English and OK at Spanish when fine-tuned or with instruction prompts; MPT can be strong for structured extraction if we template prompts properly. We'll include a language-specific eval.
[02:23] Sam: Network/security wise — we need to know whether Redwood Dedicated is required or if Hosted is acceptable. Also SSO and audit logs are requirements.
[02:31] Jordan: For the pilot we can run initial benchmarks on Hosted to speed time-to-value; if you want VPC and customer-managed keys we can spin up Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private, but that adds setup time. We'll note the tradeoffs in timeline.
[02:44] Miguel: Timeline? We pushed this as a 3-week pilot to execs. Can you run a meaningful comparison in 3 weeks?
[02:49] Priya: Yes, 3 weeks is tight but doable if we get dataset and acceptance tests in week one. Week one: data ingestion and runner setup; week two: run models and collect metrics; week three: tuning and executive review. If you need Dedicated, add 1–2 weeks for infra setup.
[03:05] Aisha: For dataset size, what's realistic? We can give 10k annotated product lines and 2k chat sessions — is that enough?
[03:12] Priya: That's within the sweet spot. For attribute extraction 10k labeled items will give decent signal; for intent accuracy 2k chats with balanced intents should be workable. We'll define sampling and holdout rules.
[03:23] Jordan: We'll also ask for a small set of typical long-context chats to validate KV cache and prefix caching behavior.
[03:30] Eva: About benchmarks: can you show both raw and tuned performance — like quantized runs vs float16? We want to see the accuracy delta vs cost delta.
[03:40] Priya: Absolutely. Our Optimize toolkit will produce cost-per-1k-token estimates, per-model quantization guidance, and a recommendation chart.
[03:47] Miguel: Aisha is also concerned about hallucinations in product descriptions — we need guardrails and evals for hallucination rate.
[03:55] Aisha: Yes — a hallucination metric would be great. Even a rough precision at 90% recall metric for attribute correctness.
[04:03] Priya: We'll include an hallucination metric: fraction of generated attributes not present in ground truth, plus examples. It's part of the evaluation harness.
[04:10] Sam: Do you support rate-limiting and circuit-breakers out of the box? For failover behavior if a model variant spikes latency?
[04:17] Jordan: Yes — Redwood routing supports fallbacks to cheaper variants, automatic throttling, and A/B canary routing. We'll put recommended policies in the runbook.
[04:27] Eva: Any data residency constraints? We have an EU store cluster and prefer EU model hosting for EU customer interactions.
[04:34] Jordan: We can host models regionally and pin requests by region; for the POC we can emulate EU hosting but for production we'd recommend Redwood Dedicated in-region or Private.
[04:44] Miguel: Ok. On the model shortlist, could you explain tradeoffs: Llama2-13B vs MPT-30B vs Falcon-40B?
[04:51] Priya: Sure. Llama2-13B (quantized) gives a good cost/quality middle ground — decent instruction-following with low token-cost when q4 quantized; MPT-30B is more template/structured-extraction friendly, often better at extraction tasks when prompts are deterministic; Falcon-40B baseline can provide higher raw quality on long prompts but at substantial compute cost; 7B options are for high-throughput low-cost needs. We'll validate on your labeled set.
[05:17] Aisha: Do you plan to do any model fine-tuning or retrieval augmentation?
[05:21] Priya: For the POC, we recommend prompt engineering plus light retrieval augmentation (RAG) against your product catalog and a few-shot approach. Full fine-tuning or RLHF is out of scope for a 3-week pilot but can be scoped later.
[05:33] Jordan: Also note that for attribute extraction a structured prompting approach or supervised fine-tune can greatly increase F1; we'll show both prompt-only and a quick supervised adaptor if time permits.
[05:43] Miguel: About privacy — do you support customer-managed keys and audit logs?
[05:48] Jordan: Yes: KMS/HSM integrations are part of Redwood Private; for Hosted we have encryption at rest and in transit and audit logs, but customer-managed keys require Dedicated/Private. We'll include a security matrix.
[05:59] Eva: On cost estimates per model — can you give a ballpark for token cost differences?
[06:04] Priya: Ballpark: 7B quantized run maybe 1 unit, 13B q4 maybe 2–3x that, 30–40B models can be 6–10x depending on eff. We'll put exact numbers in the benchmark results since runtime configs and batching affect unit costs a lot.
[06:19] Sam: For the runner, we need p95 reporting and memory/CPU logs. Can Redwood's console export those?
[06:25] Jordan: Yes, the Console provides token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, p50/p95, and tracing hooks you can ingest into your observability stack.
[06:33] Aisha: For the multilingual eval, will you do per-language splits?
[06:37] Priya: Yes, we'll split test sets by language and report top-line and per-lang metrics. If Spanish degrades, we can consider language-specific prompting or a small fine-tune.
[06:47] Miguel: Any licensing concerns with the suggested models? We prefer permissive licenses.
[06:51] Priya: We'll include license notes per model; Llama2 is generally permissive for commercial use with some terms, Falcon is also permissive, MPT has licenses depending on variant. We'll mark any restrictions.
[07:03] Eva: Regarding evaluation criteria, can we define pass/fail thresholds?
[07:06] Jordan: Proposed POC acceptance: attribute extraction F1 >= 0.88; chat intent top-1 >= 90%; p95 latency <= 300ms for assistant flows on Hosted baseline with our batching; cost per 10k tokens below your threshold or within X% of target. Those are negotiable but let's use them as starting success criteria.
[07:26] Aisha: That works as a starting point.
[07:28] Miguel: On instrumentation — we'll want to run representative traffic; are you able to replay logs for realistic load?
[07:33] Priya: Yes, we can ingest chat logs and replay at scale to measure throughput and tail latency. We'll annotate tokenization differences.
[07:40] Sam: For VPC peering, what's needed?
[07:42] Jordan: We'll share VPC peering doc and network port list; Sam you'll need to confirm a CIDR and firewall rules.
[07:51] Eva: Are you doing any adversarial tests for hallucinations or prompt injection?
[07:56] Priya: We'll include simple prompt-injection tests and check for hallucination rates on the attribute tasks. For the chat assistant we'll add safety filters and a fallback to template responses for high-uncertainty answers.
[08:07] Miguel: Good. Anything else we need to prep?
[08:09] Jordan: The main things: sample data + labels, a list of representative chat flows, and any hard latency/cost constraints you must hit. We'll draft a one-page POC plan.
[08:20] Aisha: We'll upload data by next Thursday.
[08:22] Jordan: Great. Quick note — some transcription: "K-V cache" might appear in our notes as "K V cats" so watch for that in the rough doc.
[08:30] (laughter)
[08:33] Priya: Okay let's talk about expected deliverables from Redwood for the first week: 1) model shortlist and baseline cost estimates, 2) benchmark harness (runner) with templates for the tests, 3) security and network checklist.
[08:46] Jordan: We'll also include a sample prompt pack for attribute extraction and one for chat flows.
[08:50] Miguel: On the runner, will you parameterize batching and sequence lengths? We have shorter queries for chat (avg 80 tokens) and long catalog descriptions (avg 1200 tokens).
[08:59] Priya: Yes — runner will allow profiles per workload: short-chat profile and long-batch profile. Batching behavior and KV cache hits will be separate dimensions.
[09:08] Sam: We probably want to test large sequence lengths and see memory impact; can you include tokenization reports?
[09:12] Priya: Yes, tokenization and peak GPU memory metrics are included.
[09:16] Eva: For the POC closure, what's the typical output? Exec summary + recommendations?
[09:20] Jordan: Executive summary, per-model scorecard (latency/accuracy/cost), recommended path to production (hosted vs dedicated), and an optional estimate for optimization steps (quantization, distillation, or fine-tune).
[09:31] Miguel: Ok. Let's talk about potential risks: model drift and monitoring — do you offer quality regression alerts?
[09:35] Priya: Redwood Optimize supports quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and evals; we can set baseline checks and raise alerts on regressions.
[09:41] Aisha: We may want an automated A/B test for a short period to measure user-facing metrics. Is that supported?
[09:46] Jordan: Yes, rollouts including canary and A/B are built in. We'll help design the experiment.
[09:52] Sam: For initial runs we'll use Hosted to avoid infra lead time, but we need the option to switch to Dedicated if perf/cost demands it.
[09:58] Jordan: Noted. We'll show both Hosted baseline and a Dedicated projection.
[10:02] Eva: Ok that's helpful. Any competitors you see as direct?
[10:06] Priya: Customers sometimes evaluate Anthropic, Cohere, and internal self-hosted stacks. We'll include that context.
[10:12] Miguel: Perfect. Let's make sure the security doc is comprehensive; we'll want SOC2, encryption, data retention, and the option for SAML/SSO.
[10:21] Jordan: We'll send those docs.
[10:23] Aisha: One more question — do you support generating structured JSON outputs for attributes?
[10:27] Priya: Yep. We'll test schema-constrained outputs (either via function-calling style or instruction-following to produce valid JSON).
[10:34] Miguel: Great. Anything else?
[10:36] Jordan: Quick recap and next steps — I'll email the shortlist & benchmark plan by 2025-09-02; Priya will prepare the runner and test templates; Aisha to upload data 9/4; we'll meet 9/8 for kickoff.
[10:49] Eva: Works for me.
[10:51] Miguel: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:53] Priya: Thanks all.
[10:55] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up with notes and links.
notes: Meeting had realistic transcription artifacts: occasional mis-heard acronyms (e.g., K V cats for KV cache), filler words, and brief crosstalk. The call was AE+SE-led. Customer prioritized Spanish multilingual quality, latency and cost targets, and security/compliance. POC acceptance criteria were tentatively defined and a 3-week timeline discussed with Hosted baseline and Dedicated option if needed.
